picks.why: Fills the frame with simple chunky tanks and plain straps. No extra handle or fabric texture as in 3, and no bottom nozzle holes that clash with the top flames as in 2.
Cleanest body with big simple forms. Reads instantly as a hover car, without the mouth-like grille of 1 or the extra door and hood seams of 3.
Matte, solid nucleus with the least halo glow, closest to the real cards' restrained lighting. Orbits are clear and it fills the frame well.
Balanced panels and a chunky rounded body with clean silver struts. The left panel in 2 is oversized, and 3 looks softer and washed out.
Calmest liquid with moderate bubbles and true flask proportions. 2 adds fizz up the neck and pushes saturation, and 1 is busier at the surface.
Simplest panel layout, with reels, one control strip and one vent. 1 invents a top light bar and split doors, and 2 stacks an extra button row.
Big simple arm segments with a plain base and clear gripper. 2 adds inset panel lines, and 3 adds an extra wrist segment.
Three-quarter staging matches the real cards, and the handset, cord and screen all read clearly. In 1 the handset placement weakens the read, and in 3 the cord is cramped.
Plainer background keeps focus on the pod, with solid base proportions. 1 invents a window and pillar behind it and sits tight to the top edge.
Only candidate. It is a clean, simple domed building that reads as a lab.
